newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher on fund covering.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher on fund covering.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended solidly higher Monday, on moderate volumes, as the complex continued to recover from the decline to multi-month lows in late October, traders said.
"It was mostly a light short covering rally by funds, with stops going off above $382 in December gold," FIMAT floor trader John Tyree said.
"The complex looks strong short term, but I'm not sure its the end of the downtrend yet," he said.
COMEX December gold closed up $2.30 an ounce at $382.80, its highest level for a week, after breaching resistance at last Thursday's high at $382.00, on total estimated volume of 25,000 lots.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $381.50/381.90 an ounce, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $380.50, and Friday's New York close at $379.20/379/70.
COMEX December silver ended up 5.5 cents at $4.893 an ounce, after breaching resistance at $4.875-4.880 set by intraday highs seen last Thursday and the previous Thursday.
The expiration of December gold and silver options Friday was accompanied by heavy buying of February $390 gold call options, which added a bullish tone to the market Monday, traders said.
The ongoing retreat of the U.S. dollar, from 42 month highs against the yen seen last week, also aided precious metals, analysts said, as it was seen boosting demand in Asia.
The strength of the dollar had depressed gold demand in Japan this year, with Japanese gold imports down down 49 pct to 108.3 tonnes in the January-to-September period.
"But upside price potential appears limited without much improved demand from fabricators or investors," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
Early indications of Indian demand during the Festival of Diwali on November 10 were disappointing, analysts said, and could be 20-40 percent down on last year.

"Weaker-than-anticipated physical demand, continued bullish sentiment toward financial assets and uncertainties over selling pressure from central banks and producers are expected to keep the nearby gold futures bounded between $370 and $390 through year-end," Rinehimer said.
Spot gold saw a 19 month low at $376.80 in late October.
Silver was the more volatile metal Monday, pushing the spot gold/silver ratio down further to close at 79.01, after seeing an 18 month high at 80 last week.
The partial recovery in silver followed a slide in spot silver in the bullion market to 18 month lows at $4.72 last Wednesday.

"Prospects for the sixth successive annual supply deficit in 1996, indications of strengthening demand in Asia, and COMEX silver stocks down to their lowest levels since the mid-1980s recently, suggest limited downside potential for silver," Rinehimer said.
NYMEX January platinum closed up $4.00 an ounce at $391.00, after seeing a fresh life-of-contract low at $382.00 last week, while NYMEX December palladium was unchanged at $118.00.
Spot platinum saw 35 month lows at $378.25 an ounce earlier this month, while palladium saw 43 month lows at $114.00.
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
